fixes.row: An everlasting covenant; a covenant of peace
fixes.why: Two different phrases (olam, everlasting; shalom, peace) are joined by a semicolon in one 25-verse row, so a reader takes them as one thing. The row also files Heb 13:20 (Greek aionios, eternal) with the Hebrew phrase as if it were its quotation; the Hebrew Scriptures should be heard first.
fixes.fix: Split into 'An everlasting covenant' and 'A covenant of peace' (or keep one row but state in the note that these are two phrases); list Heb 13:20 after the Hebrew verses and say in the note that its Greek word is a different word.

fixes.row: Written on the heart; the Spirit and My words
fixes.why: The label joins two separate things. Isa 59:21 speaks of My Spirit and My words in the mouth, with nothing about the heart; Jer 31:33 and Heb 8:10 say nothing of the Spirit. 2 Cor 3:6 (the Spirit versus the letter) reads the two together, a later reading in the row's own frame. Also Jer 31:31-34 is cut across the new covenant, Israel, law, heart and Egypt rows, so the teacher cannot see the one passage whole.
fixes.fix: Relabel so each part says only what its verses say: 'My laws on their hearts' (Jer 31:33; Heb 8:10, 10:16), and move Isa 59:21 and 2 Cor 3:6 to a separate row 'My Spirit and My words; the Spirit, not the letter' or to 'Every other use'. Add to the note of 'A new covenant' that Jer 31:31-34 also stands in the rows on Egypt, Israel, law and heart, so the passage can be read in sequence.

fixes.row: A new covenant; the first covenant, the old covenant
fixes.why: Jer 31:31 is the only Hebrew use of the phrase; the Greek uses are quotations or Paul's own phrase. The row mixes them without saying that 'the old covenant' (2 Cor 3:14) and 'the first covenant' (Heb 9:15) are New Testament names that the Hebrew text does not use. A reader could think the Hebrew called the Sinai covenant old.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: the Hebrew text says 'a new covenant' only at Jer 31:31; 'old covenant' and 'first covenant' are phrases of Paul and of Hebrews, not of the Hebrew Scriptures.

fixes.row: The covenants, two covenants, a better covenant; Jesus its guarantor and mediator
fixes.why: Gal 4:24 'two covenants' is an allegory of Hagar and Sinai against the Jerusalem above, not a count of covenants; the plural in Rom 9:4 and Eph 2:12 gives no number. 'Guarantor' is Heb 7:22 only, 'mediator' is 8:6, 9:15, 12:24.
fixes.fix: Keep the label; add one sentence to the note that Gal 4:24 gives 'two covenants' as an allegory of Hagar and Sinai, and that the plural in Rom 9:4 and Eph 2:12 gives no number.

fixes.row: Between people and nations: made, sworn and forbidden
fixes.why: Ps 83:5 (an alliance against God) is neither made, sworn nor forbidden in the sense of the label. The row also puts treaties and the 'make no covenant with them' commands under one heading, faithful to the one Hebrew word but reading in the Berean as two meanings.
fixes.fix: Relabel 'Between people and nations: made, sworn, forbidden, and plotted against God' or move Ps 83:5 to Every other use; add a one-line note that the Berean prints treaty, alliance or covenant for this one Hebrew word.

fixes.row: The blood of the covenant, the cup, the sacrifice
fixes.why: Dan 9:27 has no blood or cup and sits here only for 'sacrifice'. The note also puts the Lord's Supper question ahead of the Hebrew verses, so Exod 24:8 and Zech 9:11 are heard through the later question.
fixes.fix: Move Dan 9:27 to 'Every other use' (keeping its note line); in the note describe Exod 24:8 and Zech 9:11 first on their own terms, then the Gospel and Corinthian verses.

fixes.why: 87 verses of the same stories already in the named covenant rows; the reader sees them twice and may count 87 covenants.
fixes.fix: Keep (the verb idiom is the text's own) but add that most of these verses are also under the named covenants above, so the two sets overlap.

worker_points.point: Heb 8:7, 8:13, 9:1, 9:18: the Berean prints covenant where the Greek has no noun
worker_points.why: Excluding them and saying so is true to the text; the note states it clearly.
Heb 7:22, 8:6, 12:24 name Jesus and 9:15 Christ; placed by hand in the text's words. Add the Gal 4:24 note.

worker_points.point: Dan 9:27 kept in the blood/sacrifice row
worker_points.why: It has no blood or cup; move it to Every other use.

worker_points.point: Heb 9:16-17 'will' row of two verses kept on purpose
worker_points.why: Honest about one Greek word and two English words; takes no side.

worker_points.point: Patriarchs row includes the Gen 17 verses that say 'you'; circumcision
worker_points.why: The note says which verses name Abram only in 17:1; Gen 17:10-14 are in the sign row.
Berean wording stands; an optional one-line note that readers part on whether Adam is the man or a place, the page not choosing.

worker_points.point: Between people and nations puts treaty and the forbidden covenants in one row
worker_points.why: Ps 83:5 does not fit made, sworn, forbidden; relabel or move it.

worker_points.point: Israel row 52 and ark row 49 dominate
worker_points.why: They are the plain counts of the Hebrew, not a tilt.

worker_points.point: Isa 42:6 cannot be added by the builder
worker_points.why: Isa 42:6 (a covenant for the people, a light to the nations) is the Hebrew root of the nations row; its absence is a gap in the arc.

missing.what: Isa 42:6 'a covenant for the people, a light to the nations' (prefix-split, in no row); belongs in the nations row

The marriage covenant, a recurring use of the same Hebrew word with no row or note (Mal 2:14 in Every other use, Prov 2:17 in Remember/forget, Ezek 16:8 in the oath row); a row 'The covenant and marriage' would show the arc
Mal 3:1 'the messenger of the covenant' only in Every other use; fits the Levi and priests arc (Mal 2:4-8)

examples_checked: 26 of 26 rows' examples show their label (read in the Berean: Jer 33:20, Job 31:1, Gen 15:18, Gen 21:27, Neh 13:29, Deut 33:9, Ps 50:5, Ps 78:10, Hos 8:1, Josh 8:33, Heb 9:4, Acts 3:25, Lev 2:13; the rest checked against the row notes and verse lists). Ps 83:5 and Dan 9:27 fit their labels only loosely.
summary: The hub keeps the text's words, places the divine persons by hand and handles the Heb 8:7 and 9:16-17 problems honestly. It needs a split of everlasting and peace, a relabel of the heart and Spirit row, a note that old and first covenant are New Testament names, and room for the marriage covenant and Isa 42:6.
